title: Albert Einstein: Relativity's Genius
description: Relativity, awards, and the mind that reimagined the cosmos.

questions.question: Which physicist published special relativity in 1905 while employed at the Swiss patent office in Bern?
questions.explanation: His official title: "technical expert, third class." In 1905, his "miracle year," he published four landmark papers in about seven months—at 26, with no university job.

questions.question: A short 1905 follow-up paper gave Einstein his most famous equation—what is it?
questions.explanation: The paper ran three pages: "Does the Inertia of a Body Depend Upon Its Energy Content?" He didn't even write E=mc²; he used L for energy and V for the speed of light.

questions.question: Fame from E=mc² aside, Einstein's Nobel Prize honored his explanation of how light knocks electrons out of metal—called what?
questions.explanation: The Nobel committee pointedly sidestepped relativity, still seen as unproven. Einstein's reply: his 1923 Nobel lecture in Gothenburg was about relativity anyway.

questions.question: That photoelectric effect work earned Einstein the Nobel in what year?
questions.explanation: The 1921 prize was held over and announced in Nov. 1922, while he sailed to Japan. The money was already spoken for: his divorce deal had promised it to his ex-wife, Mileva.

questions.question: After his 1921 Nobel, Einstein fled Germany and spent his last 22 years at what independent research center in Princeton?
questions.explanation: Common mix-up: he was never a Princeton University professor; the institute was independent. When he died in Princeton in 1955, the pathologist removed his brain without permission.
